label: rejected

evidence.V1: Anvil-on-stump reads from front, 3/4, top and silhouette (horn + face T-profile over a banded round stump); anvil waist centred on the stump and seated (anvil_on_stump gap 0, A15 Y 0.0).
evidence.V2: Clear: stump and anvil face block (big), waist/foot and horn, iron hoops (medium), hardy hole and cream stump-top ring (small).
evidence.V3: Anvil body is a straight box T with a plain cone horn and no waisting or curved horn underside; the stump flare helps but the anvil reads as stiff primitives.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on face block, foot plate, stump rims and hoops catch light in face and stump close-ups.
evidence.V5: Horn surface is uneven: wavy/lumpy outline and shading where the cone meets the body (horn studio + flat close-ups); stump shows strong flat 12-sided facets that read as low-poly rather than designed bark.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: steel grey anvil in 2 values, wood stump in 2 values, ink iron hoops, cream end-grain ring; colourways only change the stump.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, steel greys, ink iron and chamfers match, but the hard-faceted stump departs from the kit's smooth weighted-normal shading.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre; all gates pass.

evidence.V1: Classic anvil-on-stump outline (horn, face, waist, banded stump) reads from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette; A15 Y error 0.0 and the waist is centred over the stump.
evidence.V2: Big anvil + stump masses, medium waist foot and iron bands, small hardy hole and cream cut-face ring - clear layering.
evidence.V3: Anvil body is a straight-sided box with a plain cone horn and the stump a straight faceted cylinder with a slight flare; only partly stylised (no chunky taper, flared heel or chunky horn curve).
evidence.V4: Anvil face, waist and foot carry consistent chamfers that catch light, but the 12-sided stump has hard, unsoftened facet edges and the horn meets the body with an un-bevelled step.
evidence.V5: Stump shows stripe-like flat faceting in the studio close-ups and colourways, and the horn-to-body junction shows a pinched shading seam in close_horn_studio.
evidence.V6: Steel grey in two values for the anvil, wood brown stump, ink iron bands, cream cut face - disciplined.
evidence.V7: 1120 tris vs medium target 2000: under target.
evidence.V8: Kit palette and anvil chamfers match, but the visibly faceted low-segment stump departs from the smooth weighted-normal kit look.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, bottom-centre origin, MeshPart white with vertex colours.

evidence.V1: Horned anvil on a hooped stump reads clearly in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view still reads via horn + rectangular face + hardy hole.
evidence.V2: Big (stump), medium (anvil body, horn, two iron hoops, foot plinth), small (hardy hole, cream cut-ring on the stump) hierarchy is clear.
evidence.V3: Horn and flared foot help, but the body and waist are straight rectangular blocks with no heel taper or waist pinch, so the anvil reads partly as stiff primitives.
evidence.V4: Anvil face and foot carry consistent chamfers, but the stump is a hard-edged 16-sided prism whose polygon edges read razor-like instead of bevelled.
evidence.V5: Stump shows stray faceting (flat polygon bands in the stump-top close-up), and the horn joins the body as a narrower cone stepping out of the body face in the horn close-up.
evidence.V6: Steel grey anvil in 2-3 values, one wood hue for the stump, ink hoops, cream cut-ring; disciplined.
evidence.V8: Steel greys, ink iron and wood match the kit palette, but the hard faceted stump departs from the smooth weighted-normal, chamfered kit finish.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre; A1-A18 pass, Y symmetry 0.0.

artifacts: Wavy/lumpy horn surface and outline near its root
Hard flat faceting on the round stump
Visible flat faceting stripes on the 12-sided stump
Pinched shading / hard step where the cone horn meets the anvil body
horn-to-body step where the cone base is narrower than the body end
top_fixes: Rebuild the horn as a smooth, slightly downward-curving taper that blends into the face block
Give the anvil a waisted body (concave sides, flared foot) and a step/table under the face for a confident stylised profile
Smooth the stump (more segments or weighted normals) or make the facets deliberate bark planks
Raise stump segments or smooth-shade it with weighted normals so it reads round, and add growth rings / bark lip for a stump read
Fuse the horn into the body with a curved transition and a slight upward sweep instead of a plain cone
Give the anvil body a flared heel and waisted taper so it reads less like a box primitive
Smooth the stump (more segments or weighted normals with a soft chamfer) so it reads as a rounded log
Blend the horn into the body with a matching cross-section instead of a cone stepping out of the face
Pinch the waist and taper the heel so the anvil body reads less like stacked boxes
